titulo: Partizip I and II as adjectives: Partizip I as an adjective

aula.titulo: Partizip I and II as adjectives
aula.objetivo: Use the Partizip II (gekochte Eier, ein verlorener Schlüssel, die gestiegenen Preise) and the Partizip I (lachend, die spielenden Kinder) as adjectives, with the right ending and the right meaning (passive and completed, active and completed, or active and ongoing).

blocos.titulo: The Partizip I as an adjective, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the PARTIZIP I is the INFINITIVE + «-D»: lachen → lachend; laufen → laufend; schlafen → schlafend; spielen → spielend. It is the German counterpart of the English -ing adjective ("a laughing child"). STEP 2: the MEANING is ACTIVE and ONGOING: «das schlafende Kind» is the child WHO IS SLEEPING; «die spielenden Kinder», the children who are playing. STEP 3: before the noun it takes adjective endings: «ein lachendes Kind», «die spielenden Kinder», «fließendes Wasser». STEP 4: it can work as an ADVERB, with no ending: «Er kam lachend herein» (he came in laughing). Careful: German never uses the Partizip I for the English continuous tense — "I am laughing" is «ich lache», never «ich bin lachend». STEP 5: it appears in fixed expressions: «laufende Kosten» (running costs), «steigende Preise» (rising prices), «fließend Deutsch sprechen» (to speak German fluently). STEP 6: compare: Partizip I (active, happening) × Partizip II (passive, completed): «das kochende Wasser» (the boiling water) × «das gekochte Ei» (the boiled egg).

tabela.exemplo: das kochende Wasser × das gekochte Ei
